name: Hòn Mun
kicker: The reef you snorkel or dive
summary: Coral island in the bay: snorkel or dive the reef on a 45-minute boat from Cầu Đá for the marine reserve. The reef is why you leave the city sand. Glass-bottom boats are the dry way to see the coral. About 350 coral species grow here.
getThere: 45 minutes by boat from Cầu Đá.
heroCaption: People in the clear water along the Hòn Mun shore
body: Hòn Mun is the snorkel and dive stop in the bay. The boat from Cầu Đá port takes 45 minutes. Glass-bottom boats are the way to see the reef without getting in. The shore itself is rocks, huts, and clear water.

About 350 coral species grow at Hòn Mun, more than 40 percent of the world’s hard corals. The water was planned as Vietnam’s first marine protected area, and the island is also the country’s only protected marine reserve, a marine biodiversity area recognised by the World Wildlife Fund. Come in the dry months, January to August. Diving on this coast is popular from January through October.

gettingThere: The boat leaves Cầu Đá port and takes 45 minutes. Pay the bay scenic fee before you board, then the boat fare on top.

legs.heading: From Cầu Đá
legs.body: A 45-minute boat. The scenic fee for the Hòn Mun route is 10,000 VND a person each crossing, plus 3,000 VND for the pier.

legs.heading: From Trần Phú
legs.body: Ride south along the beach road to Cầu Đá, then take the boat.

admissionNote: The boat fare is separate. The scenic fee is 10,000 VND a person each crossing to Hòn Mun, plus 3,000 VND at the pier. It follows the crossing from the inland pier and excludes accident insurance. Children under 6 and Khánh Hòa residents are among those exempt. A child from 6 to under 16 pays half. A combined ticket for every listed route is 40,000 VND.
